author: reek
body: Every test that waits on a keystroke is skipped, and the skip reasons say so plainly -- "blocks waiting for keyboard input", "requires display + keyboard". The reason was never that the VM cannot deliver a key: codex-vm has taken a scancode timeline through `-keys-file` for as long as build/test-gui.ps1 has driven GUI apps with one. It was that the default battery had no sidecar for it, so the only input a test could ask for was `.stdin`, and `.stdin` cannot reach a keyboard read at all: it is pumped into the serial ring, and `poll-key` reads the PS/2 key cell. Two paths, and the battery only had the wrong one.

author: reek
body: This test drives the second path. Its `.keys` sidecar types a, b and Enter as Set-1 make codes (30, 48, 28); the loop below is the shape `idm-rlb-loop` uses, and it must report 97, 98 and stop -- lowercase, because no shift was pressed and `poll-key` now decodes shift. The shift decode itself is pinned by `codex/test/keys-shift`.

author: reek
body: There is no fuel cap. A loop that never sees a key hangs until the harness's wall budget kills it, which is the honest failure: this test exists to prove keys arrive, so not arriving must be a failure and not a quietly truncated answer.
